answer: Divergent History Attestation. Each identity periodically signs a crystal of its recent action log plus a nonce; the registry rejects any two identities whose logs share a ripple of identical action hashes over a rolling window. Clones replaying the same behavior produce matching hashes and get flagged. To pass, an attacker must inject a unique delta into every clone's action history and sustain it, paying separate real task execution, storage, and signing costs per identity indefinitely.
